summary: Zambia's Department of Immigration lists the nationalities that need no visa — including the US, UK and the EU — and entitles visitors to 90 days in any 12 months. Other nationalities can either get a visa on arrival or from a Zambian mission, or must have a visa approved online before travel; the KAZA UniVisa covers Zambia and Zimbabwe around Victoria Falls.

tips.text: Visiting both sides of Victoria Falls? The UK Foreign Office says the KAZA UniVisa costs 50 US dollars, is valid for 30 days, and allows unlimited travel between Zambia and Zimbabwe plus day trips to Botswana. It is sold at Lusaka and Livingstone airports and at the Victoria Falls and Kazungula land borders.

The Government of Canada says malaria is a risk in Zambia and antimalarial medication is recommended for most travellers; see a health professional or travel clinic before you go, and protect yourself from mosquito bites.
The UK Foreign Office says it is dangerous to drive outside the main towns after dark because of abandoned vehicles, pedestrians and stray animals on the road, and vehicles driven without lights.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Zambia?
faq.answer: Not if your nationality is on the Department of Immigration's list of nationalities that need no visa, which includes the US, UK, EU members, Canada, Australia and Japan. Visitors may stay up to 90 days in any 12 months. Other nationalities either can get a visa on arrival or from a Zambian mission, or must have a visa approved through the official Zambia Immigration e-services portal before travel.

faq.question: What is the KAZA UniVisa?
faq.answer: A joint Zambia–Zimbabwe visa costing USD 50, valid up to 30 days in any 12 months, available to eligible nationalities at Lusaka and Livingstone airports and the Victoria Falls and Kazungula borders, or online in advance for arrival at those Zambian ports. It allows multiple visits to both countries and day trips into Botswana through Kazungula.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Zambia?
faq.answer: Zambia's Department of Immigration says ordinary visitors, business visitors and tourists are entitled to a free 90-day visit in any 12 months, counted from the day of first entry. The days may not all be given at once; the rest can be added free of charge at the nearest immigration office.

faq.question: How do I get a Zambia eVisa and what does it cost?
faq.answer: Apply at eservices.zambiaimmigration.gov.zm, where you register an account, complete the visa form, upload documents and pay by card. A single-entry visa costs USD 25. The Department of Immigration says to bring the approval letter and receipt when you travel; no processing time is published.

faq.answer: The UK government says you need a yellow fever certificate if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.
